title: Asking to push the plan
situation: You're too wiped out for tomorrow's plan, so you text a friend to push it to next week.
tip: When you bail, soften it: a quick 미안 + a reason + offering a new day keeps it casual and not flaky. Tossing back 언제가 좋아? hands them the choice.

turns.en: What time should we meet tomorrow?

turns.prompt: Apologize and ask to push it to next week.

choices.ko: 아 미안ㅠ 나 내일 말고 담주에 보면 안 될까?
choices.en: Ah sorry ㅠ could we do next week instead of tomorrow?
choices.feedback: 미안 + 담주 (next week) + a soft 안 될까? is exactly how friends ask to reschedule.

choices.en: I'm sorry but I would like to change our appointment.
choices.feedback: Way too formal — 죄송하지만/변경하다 sounds like a business email, not a friend.

choices.en: What time should we meet tomorrow?
choices.feedback: That just repeats their question instead of asking to move the plan.

turns.ko: 오 그래 괜찮아~ 무슨 일 있어?
turns.en: Oh sure, no problem~ is something up?

choices.en: No, I've just been so tired lately ㅠㅠ
choices.feedback: 그냥 + a real reason is natural and honest — friends don't need a big excuse.

choices.en: There is no particular reason.
choices.feedback: 사유/없습니다 is stiff bureaucratic Korean — friends say 그냥.

choices.en: Is something up with you lately?
choices.feedback: Flips the question back at them instead of answering — doesn't fit.

turns.ko: 헐 푹 쉬어ㅠ 그럼 담주 언제가 좋아?
turns.en: Aw get some rest ㅠ so when next week works for you?

turns.prompt: Suggest the weekend and bounce it back.

choices.en: How about the weekend? Saturday or Sunday!
choices.feedback: A concrete option (토욜/일욜) plus 어때? keeps the rescheduling moving.

choices.en: I am available on the weekend.
choices.feedback: 가능합니다 is too formal — with a friend just say 주말 어때?

choices.en: Yeah I'll rest well, thanks.
choices.feedback: Polite, but it drops the ball — they asked which day, so you should pick one.

turns.prompt: Confirm and thank them for understanding.

choices.en: Okay, Saturday! Thanks for understanding hehe
choices.feedback: 오키 + confirming the day + a quick thanks is a warm, natural sign-off.

choices.en: Thank you for your understanding (formal).
choices.feedback: 양해/감사합니다 is customer-service formal — too stiff for a friend.

choices.en: Saturday's kind of iffy.
choices.feedback: Contradicts what you both just agreed on — confusing.

title: Warning you'll be late
situation: You're stuck and running about 20 minutes late, so you text the friend already waiting.
tip: Give a heads-up early with a time (한 20분), a reason, and what they should do meanwhile (먼저 들어가 있어). 미안 ㅠ goes a long way.

turns.en: Hey, where are you? I'm here.

turns.prompt: Warn them you'll be about 20 min late and say sorry.

choices.ko: 헉 미안ㅠ 나 한 20분 늦을 거 같아
choices.en: Oh no, sorry ㅠ I think I'll be about 20 min late
choices.feedback: Heads-up with a number (한 20분) + 미안 is exactly the right move when you're running late.

choices.en: My arrival is expected to be delayed.
choices.feedback: 지연/예정입니다 reads like a train announcement — friends say 늦을 거 같아.

choices.en: Where are you?
choices.feedback: Just echoes their question — doesn't tell them you're late.

turns.prompt: Explain the bus is super late.

choices.en: The bus isn't coming ㅠ I'm seriously losing it
choices.feedback: A real, vivid reason + 미치겠다 sounds like a frustrated friend in the moment.

choices.en: I am late due to public transit circumstances.
choices.feedback: 사정으로 인하여 is formal/written — nobody texts a friend like this.

choices.en: Yeah, did something happen?
choices.feedback: Bounces the question back instead of explaining why you're late.

turns.en: Ah it's fine lol take your time~

turns.prompt: Tell them to go in first and order without you.

choices.ko: ㅇㅇ 먼저 들어가 있어! 음료 먼저 시켜 놔ㅋㅋ
choices.en: Yeah, go in first and order a drink while you wait lol
choices.feedback: 먼저 들어가 있어 + 음료 먼저 시켜 놔 naturally gives your waiting friend something to do.

choices.en: Please enter ahead of me (formal).
choices.feedback: 입장/바랍니다 is announcement-speak — say 먼저 들어가 있어.

choices.en: How's the vibe at that cafe?
choices.feedback: Random subject change — doesn't deal with you being late.

turns.en: Okay lol got it, hurry up

turns.prompt: Say you're almost there and apologize again.

choices.ko: 거의 다 왔어! 금방 갈게 미안ㅠ
choices.en: Almost there! I'll be quick, sorry ㅠ
choices.feedback: 거의 다 왔어 + 금방 갈게 + 미안 wraps it up warmly and naturally.

choices.en: I will move as swiftly as possible (formal).
choices.feedback: 신속히/이동하겠습니다 is way too formal for a friend.

choices.en: I'll take my time getting there.
choices.feedback: Wrong meaning — you're late, so saying you'll go slowly doesn't fit.

title: Bailing because you feel off
situation: You feel sick the day of the plan and text a friend to cancel and do it another time.
tip: Canceling for your health: state it simply (컨디션이 안 좋아), apologize, and lock in 다음에 so it doesn't feel like a brush-off. 다음에 내가 살게 is a sweet way to make up for it.

turns.en: We're still on for tonight, right?

turns.prompt: Say you're not feeling great and ask to do it another time.

choices.ko: 미안ㅠ 나 오늘 컨디션이 너무 안 좋아서 다음에 보면 안 될까?
choices.en: Sorry ㅠ I'm really not feeling well today, can we meet another time?
choices.feedback: 컨디션이 안 좋아 + 다음에 + 안 될까? is the standard, kind way to cancel and reschedule.

choices.en: I am canceling today's appointment due to poor condition.
choices.feedback: 금일/난조/취소합니다 is formal written Korean — robotic for a friend.

choices.en: We're still on for tonight, right?
choices.feedback: Just repeats their line instead of canceling.

turns.en: Oh no, are you sick? You okay?

turns.prompt: Say you think you caught a cold.

choices.ko: 감기 걸렸나 봐ㅠ 목도 아프고 으슬으슬해
choices.en: I think I caught a cold ㅠ my throat hurts and I've got the chills
choices.feedback: 감기 걸렸나 봐 + symptoms is natural — gives them a clear, relatable picture.

choices.en: It is surmised that I have contracted a cold (formal).
choices.feedback: 이환/사료됩니다 is medical-report language — absurd in a text to a friend.

choices.en: You're not sick?
choices.feedback: Turns it around onto them instead of answering how you feel.

turns.ko: 아이고ㅠ 약 먹고 푹 자 진짜
turns.en: Aww ㅠ take some meds and really get some sleep

turns.prompt: Thank them and promise to treat them next time.

choices.ko: ㅇㅇ 약 먹고 잘게ㅠ 다음엔 내가 살게!
choices.en: Yeah I'll take meds and sleep ㅠ next time it's on me!
choices.feedback: Reacts to their advice (약 먹고 잘게) then offers 다음엔 내가 살게 — makes up for bailing and keeps it warm.

choices.en: I deeply appreciate your consideration (formal).
choices.feedback: 배려/감사드립니다 is far too formal — friends just say 고마워.

choices.en: Forget the meds, I'll just sleep.
choices.feedback: Brushes off their kind advice — sounds a bit cold.

turns.en: Yeah, let's meet once you're better! Take good care

turns.prompt: Agree and tell them you'll text when you're better.

choices.en: Yeah I'll message you as soon as I'm better! Thanks hehe
choices.feedback: 나으면 바로 연락할게 confirms the rain check and ends on a warm note.

choices.en: I will contact you as soon as I recover (formal).
choices.feedback: 쾌차/연락드리겠습니다 is too polite/formal for a close friend.

choices.en: I'm already all better lol
choices.feedback: Contradicts the whole reason you canceled — confusing.
